questiontext.text:
We have simulated data sets giving the crop yield for different crops. The outcome variable is the Crop Yield, and the explanatory variables are:

  • Soil Quality Index Score - a numerical variable ranging from 1-10, representing soil quality, where higher scores indicate better quality.
  • Crop Planted - a factor variable indicating the type of crop planted.
  • Region - a factor variable specifying the region (North or South).
  • Density of pests in the crop - a numerical variable indicating the density of pests in the crop.
  • Pest susceptibility - a factor variable with three levels (low, medium, high) representing how susceptible the given crop is to pests.

The following visualisation shows a boxplot displaying the crop yield values, split by crop type (x axis) and region (facets).

We additionally have the points placed on the boxplot giving the colour as the pest density.

In this plot, we can see that region, pest density, and crop type are all correlated to the yield. Higher pest densities result in lower yields. Furthermore, corn and sorghum perform better in the South region than in the North Region. In fact, if in the South Region, it appears that Corn or Sorghum would result in the highest yield. However, if in the North region, then it appears that rice results in the highest yield.

We can see that the North region results in the smallest yield for Corn and Sorghum, but not for Rice. We can also see that the pest density is very high in the North region for both Corn and Sorghum and not for Rice. It is likely that these areas had a high pest density, causing the low yields.

Download this data. This is not the same as the data used to make the graphic above. Using the downloaded data, create a similar visualisation.

Which of the following statement(s) are true? Check all that apply:
